key_insight: Physics-informed neural networks discover strongly nonlinear water waves with near-machine-precision residuals, while interval arithmetic and Lean independently certify a selected candidate’s residual bound.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers an auditable route to highly accurate nonlinear wave computations relevant to free-surface flow modeling.
method: Learn periodic wave profiles, speed and optionally surface tension directly from governing equations without training data.
Use staged neural-network training and refinement to recover known wave families and explore new candidates.
Freeze one candidate, certify its uniform residual bound with interval arithmetic, and machine-check the deductions in Lean.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports recovery of Stokes waves, Crapper waves and Wilton ripples, new high-amplitude candidates from continuation, and rigorous residual certification for one candidate.
watch_item: The certified result bounds one candidate’s equation residual; it does not by itself establish existence, uniqueness or dynamical stability of an exact nearby wave.
paper_title: Rigorously Certified Neural-Network Computation of Nonlinear Water Waves at Near-Machine Precision
